thread.title: Boeing’s stock leads the charge to Dow 25,000, up about 150 points

author: Mark DeCambre
title: Boeing’s stock leads the charge to Dow 25,000, up about 150 points
text:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average broke above 25,000 for the first time in history shortly after the opening bell on Thursday, a move that comes just 23 trading days after it first closed above 24,000. That marks the fastest move ever to the next 1,000-point milestone, according WSJ Market Data Group.
The advance this time was led by Boeing Co., which contributed almost 150 points to the price-weighted average’s rally. A $1 move of any of the Dow’s DJIA, +0.60% components equates to a roughly 6.8-point swing in the equity gauge. Some of the other big contributors are Caterpillar Inc., Chevron Corp., and Home Depot. 
Expectations for an infrastructure spending bill to surface at some point in 2018, along with crude-oil prices CLG8, +0.57% rising above $60 a barrel for the first time since 2015, have helped these names lead the charge.

-52 Source: WSJ Market Data Group To be sure, the run-up to 25,000 isn’t truly significant in any technical or fundamental sense, but because the Dow represents the oldest measure of stock performance, round-number moves tend to be closely followed on Wall Street and Main Street. 
Representing around 80% of the investible U.S. equity market, the S&P 500 index SPX, +0.48% is a better representation of market performance. However, the Dow was first calculated in 1896, while the S&P 500 made its debut in present form in 1957.
